title: Category icons, receipt items sorted by your rules, and Monero
items: Pick an icon for each category from about 60 in the category form.
Receipts split into items file each line under a category from your rules, and Remember saves a rule for next time.
Every amount box takes a decimal comma, such as 12,50, in any browser.
Monero (XMR) is in the currency list, with daily rates.
Repair Data can ignore a duplicate you have checked, so it stops coming back on every scan.
Category Details says when its bars are budget months rather than calendar months.

title: Your own colours, and bills that are only paid once
items: Pick the colours for money in and money out under Settings > Colours, including a colour-blind friendly preset. Amounts, budget bars, charts and PDF exports all follow them.
A transaction's menu has Link to bill, which files a payment you entered yourself under one of your bills, so it shows in Bills by Month.
Mark Paid asks before paying anything twice. When a bill already has a payment for its date you can use that payment, and a double click only counts once.
Bills by Month shows each payment in the month it was paid and the due date it paid, and counts a payment made either side of New Year once.
Importing a CSV again with the columns mapped differently no longer adds it a second time, even after you have edited a payee.
Repair Data finds more payments that older versions recorded twice.
The Transactions list keeps its headings and page controls in view, and works better on a laptop or a phone.

title: Budget 3.0, the first release out of beta
items: Budget is out of beta. 3.0 is the first release considered stable, every part of the app was reviewed and tested ahead of it, upgrading from 2.x included, so the beta warning has gone. Making a backup from Settings every now and then is still a good idea.

There is now an Android app, Budget Companion, on Google Play. Photograph a receipt and your own server reads it (when receipt scanning is set up), add a transaction by hand when there is no receipt, and check your balances, what is left of this month's budget and the bills due. Anything you enter without a signal is sent once you are back online.
An import folder: drop a bank statement into a folder in your Files and it is imported in the background, or held for you to check first. It is set up under Settings.
Statements can be imported straight from Excel and LibreOffice (.xls, .xlsx and .ods), and exports from Firefly III, YNAB, Actual Budget, Mint and Monarch Money can be brought across.
Sharing has a Full control level as well as Read only and Read & Write, and the Budget page has a Ready to Assign card, with weekly, quarterly and yearly budgets measured over the month.
The Transactions page works on a phone, the sidebar matches the rest of Nextcloud and the app opens faster.
Someone new to Budget gets a getting started checklist, and can try it out with sample data first.

links.text: Get Budget Companion on Google Play

title: Skipping transfers and a projected balance
items: Transfers can now be skipped the same as bills, the due date moves on one cycle and Undo puts it back.
Pick an account in the Bills Calendar's Account filter and a Projected balance row shows what it should hold at the end of each month for the rest of the year.
Paid bills show the date they were paid as well as when they are next due.
A payment marked paid with no transaction behind it can be dismissed, rather than being listed for 60 days.
The import review warns about rows with no description, since import rules cannot categorise them.
